chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Not every oath requires an expiation. As for what is obligatory upon you to do, and you swear not to do it, then you do it, there is no expiation upon you for it; and as for what is not obligatory upon you to do, and you swear not to do it, then you do it, then upon you is the expiation for it.'
ai.seo_question: When does breaking an oath require expiation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between oaths concerning obligatory duties (wajib), where breaking the oath incurs no expiation because the act remains mandatory, and oaths concerning non-obligatory acts, where breaking the oath requires expiation. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the nature of the act determines the penalty, ensuring that believers are not burdened with double obligations for fulfilling what is already required by God. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the conditions under which kaffarah al-yamin applies in daily religious practice.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is not any expiation in every oath. But whatever was Obligated from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> upon you to do, so you swear that you will not do it, (and then) you do it, so there is no expiation upon you regarding it; and as for what does not happen to be from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Obligated upon you to do, so you swear that you would not do it, then you do it, so upon you is the expiation regarding it’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Mahbub from ‘ Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has narrated the following:

“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Every kind of oath does not make one liable to expiation. If the matter is what Allah has made obligatory on you to do and you take an oath not to do it but you do it there is no expiation on you. If it is not of the matters that Allah has made obligatory on you to do and you take an oath not to do it but you do it, then there is expiation on you.’”
